I lived in Japan for a while. During my stay, I visited Kyoto, and visited several shrines and temples. One was a little cave that you reached by walking down some stairs.

The path was curved, like a spiral. And you are in complete darkness. There's a stone in the middle of the cave, which you're supposed to find by keeping one hand on the wall and walking forward.

It's like returning to the womb. Utter darkness, the sounds of the city above a muted whisper. Just you and the stone close to you.

It was comforting, in a way.

I went into a cave system in CA, can't remember the name but they did guided tours.

It was really beautiful, but I found out that day that I really don't like being underground, lol.

Years later I started playing Minecraft and discovered that my dislike/fear of being underground held true even in the game! Though as long as I put down torches so I don't get lost and surface frequently I'm ok.

I admire folks that go caving, I wish I could handle it.

I have toured many caves, all but one in the north Midwest (the exception in Ireland). All where guide tours thru active caves.

I have also gone with small groups in the caves along the Mississippi river and in parts of the Black Hills. All are super cool, but for me intimidating.

I went out the way I came in! I've been to the caves in the southeast, but always with a group. There are caving groups all around and I really wouldn't recommend doing it alone. That being said it was surreal, and I've not seen or felt the same anywhere else.
